readerValueVsCompetitors.reason: The top results are Home-Barista threads ('Even at grind size 1 my Barista Express still gushes', 'Can't get Breville/Sage to grind fine enough'), the Singletrack thread and the Seattle Coffee Gear top-burr post. None of them gives an ordered diagnosis. The draft does: 'The test you can run tonight', then clean, then the upper burr 'one number toward finer', then the date code and the manufacturer, then 'the built-in grinder is the limit… buy a separate espresso grinder'.

distinctivenessVoice.reason: It opens 'Don't buy anything yet.' and commits to one view throughout. It contradicts the forum ('The manual says something different') and the retailer ('follow the ring, not the forum'). 'When I'd choose differently' now carries one label in its intro, not a label on every item.

honestyAboutLimits.reason: 'What the booklet doesn't say' states the four unknowns once. The parts listing is called 'a parts listing, not a manufacturer spec', and the owner report is 'a single report, not a spec'. The methods section says 'we did not test either machine' and 'this guide doesn't name one'.

evidenceIntegrity.reason: All the factual statements map to claims: dial ranges, the 5–20 day roast window, the dual-wall quote, the 22–33 lb tamp, flow timings, the troubleshooting causes, the PDC part numbers and the warranty wording. The 'metal on metal → back off' rule is labelled as the writer's judgement. The 'roughly 10–15 kg' conversion is our own arithmetic, not from a claim, but it's harmless.

topicFit.reason: It follows the brief's thesis exactly: free checks in order, then the upper burr, then a replacement burr through the manufacturer, and only then a separate grinder. It keeps the leaveOut items out (no '6' default, no shims, no grinder picks, no prices). The keep-yours outcome is the default ('If any step above slowed the shot… buy nothing').

competitorComparison.weGiveThatTheyDont: One ordered sequence in place of scattered replies. It rules out stale beans, the dual-wall basket and under-dosing before the burr, quotes the manufacturer's own causes for 'runs out too quickly', and sets a clear point at which to stop and buy a grinder.

The correct direction for fast shots (toward FINE, where SCG says coarser), checks to do before opening the grinder, the undocumented range and factory position stated honestly, the PDC part-number check, and the route through the warranty or manufacturer before buying.

It turns one owner's fix (clean the burrs, internal burr to 1, free burr from the manufacturer) into a general procedure grounded in the manual. It also settles the 'shim it / don't touch it / buy a grinder' split that the thread leaves open.

blockingActions: Shorten the title to 70 characters or fewer, counting the longest filled-in product name (GB names are longer). Make it one problem-first promise, not two clauses with two product tokens, e.g. 'Built-in grinder still too fast at setting 1? Check these before buying'. Keep the machine names in the description.

Add a seoTitle of 60 characters or fewer that leads with the search problem, e.g. 'Barista Express too fast at grind setting 1? Fix it first'. Check it is 60 or fewer with product names filled in if you use a token.
optionalImprovements: Publish gate for the human: build and publish the grinder-for-barista-express-and-pro guide before this post ships. Until then, 'our guide to choosing a grinder… answers it' renders as plain text and promises the reader something that doesn't exist. Grinder offers for this post also need new research: the Express and Pro portafilter size, dosing fit, and variants sold in both the US and GB.
Check the description length with product names filled in. Two product tokens may push it past what a search snippet shows.
Methods: the raw source URLs are fine in the collapsed section, but check the renderer doesn't turn them into body links that count against the two-link limit.
'dialled in' is British spelling in a post whose market field is US. That's fine for a post shown in every market, but keep the spelling consistent.
